assertions: First local lifecycle run provisions a missing environment.
Second local lifecycle deploy detects the existing environment and does not recreate it.
Reset clears application/deployed state without deleting the cluster.
Delete spins down the environment only when explicit destroy intent is set.
Skip-destroy leaves the environment active for branch reuse.
The graph asserts external lifecycle evidence through provisioning markers, scaffolded repo outputs, and downstream env context instead of relying only on node exit codes.
evidence: test_graph/sources/Tg6LocalLifecycleProvisionMissing.py provisions a missing local-preview environment through the scaffolded environment repository.
test_graph/sources/Tg6LocalLifecycleDeployExisting.py deploys an application marker into the existing local environment and asserts reuse.
test_graph/sources/Tg6LocalLifecycleDeployMarkers.py asserts provisioned/deployed markers and proves deploy reuse skipped tofu apply.
test_graph/sources/Tg6LocalLifecycleReset.py and Tg6LocalLifecycleResetMarkers.py assert reset reapplies, clears application state, keeps provisioned state, and clears deployed state.
test_graph/sources/Tg6LocalLifecycleSkipDestroy.py asserts skip-destroy keeps the environment active.
test_graph/sources/Tg6LocalLifecycleDestroy.py and Tg6LocalLifecycleDestroyMarkers.py validate guarded destroy behavior and explicit destroy marker cleanup.

assertions: GitHub Actions lifecycle graph is discoverable in normal runs and validates the local-github-action scaffold without requiring cloud infrastructure.
GitHub Actions graph covers first deploy, existing deploy reuse, reset, explicit destroy guard behavior, and skip-destroy/keep-alive behavior using CI-safe markers and context projection.
AWS lifecycle graph is discoverable in normal runs.
Without explicit selection and credentials, AWS graph records a guarded skip/fail-fast result and creates no cloud resources.
With explicit selection and AWS credentials, the graph covers first deploy, existing deploy reuse, reset, explicit destroy, and skip-destroy.
Destroy requires TEST_GRAPH_DESTROY_BRANCH_ENVIRONMENT or TESTGRAPH_DESTROY_BRANCH_ENVIRONMENT in addition to AWS selection.

assertions.Local, GitHub Actions, and AWS lifecycle: missing cluster deploy, existing cluster reuse without recreation, reset, explicit teardown, and skip teardown.
